text: The papers' own reading of the body
why: The story mentions that the papers reported the case but never gives any reading of the body from them; this label asserts a reading the story has not supplied.
¶35 describes a bowl-shaped depression immediately beyond the furze-bush area where the body lay.

text: The red and black silk cravat
why: ¶35 states that Straker clasped a red and black silk cravat in his left hand.
¶35 states that Straker's overcoat was flapping from a furze-bush.
¶35 states that Straker held a small knife in his right hand.
The story says the knife was in Straker's own hand, and nothing establishes that it was an assailant's; the label presents an unproven ownership as a name.
Straker was killed on Monday night and his wife found him missing at seven the next morning, so the body was found on Tuesday morning.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush?
why: The overcoat's position at the furze-bush is stated in ¶35, so asking how it got there is a plain question the story has raised.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush? — torn off in the struggle
why: The story describes Straker defending himself vigorously against assailants, so a struggle that tore off the coat is a possibility a reader has reason to consider.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush? — Straker took it off himself
why: Straker had pulled on a large mackintosh before leaving the house in the rain (¶32), so the possibility that he removed his coat himself is a reasonable one to consider.

text: Who struck the blow that killed Straker? — unknown assailants
why: The story mentions 'assailants' in the plural and a blow from a heavy weapon, but names no one, so 'unknown assailants' is an open possibility.

text: What made the blow to Straker's head?
why: ¶35 says the head was struck by 'some heavy weapon' that is never identified, so the question is open and plainly raised.

text: What made the cut on Straker's thigh?
why: ¶35 says the thigh cut was inflicted by 'some very sharp instrument' that is never identified, so the question is open and plainly raised.

text: What made the cut on Straker's thigh? — an assailant's very sharp instrument
why: A sharp instrument in an assailant's hand is a possibility a reader can reasonably consider given the struggle and the plural assailants, though the story does not yet say who made the cut.
